text.p: Nestle SA, the world's biggest food company, Wednesday reported 1996 group net profit rose 16.6 percent to 3.40 billion Swiss francs ($2.3 billion), helped by a weaker Swiss currency.
Nestle had already reported 1996 sales rose 7.1 percent as volume gains teamed up with the weaker Swiss franc to boost revenue expressed in the domestic currency.

Chief Financial Officer Mario Corti told Reuters Financial Television the weak currency was continuing to help lift sales this year, with revenues up by double digits in Swiss franc terms in the first two months of the year.

"Expressed in Swiss francs there is obviously very strong growth, in fact it was double-digit," Corti said. But he added it would be difficult to maintain such solid growth rates over the entire year.
